purpose: Tabular data — streamflow timeseries, signatures, model outputs, CSV I/O

DataFrame.resample.note: Requires DatetimeIndex. Always parse dates when reading: pd.read_csv(..., parse_dates=['date'], index_col='date').

DataFrame.rolling.note: min_periods=1 avoids NaN at the start of a window. Default drops incomplete windows.

gotchas: Setting values on a copy: df[df['q'] > 0]['flag'] = 1 silently does nothing. Use df.loc[df['q'] > 0, 'flag'] = 1.
Integer dtype with NaN: int columns become float64 when NaN is present. Use pd.Int64Dtype() for nullable integers.
Chained indexing: df['a']['b'] can raise SettingWithCopyWarning — use df.loc[:, ('a', 'b')] or df[['a']]['b'].
Date parsing timezone: pd.to_datetime() without utc=True drops timezone info. For NWIS data, use pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True).dt.tz_convert(None) to strip tz.
resample vs groupby: resample('ME') (month-end) vs groupby(df.index.month) give different alignment for irregular timeseries.
Pandas 2.0 removed append(): use pd.concat([df1, df2], ignore_index=True) instead.
Copy-on-Write (pandas 2.0+): modifying a slice modifies a copy — use .copy() explicitly if you need an independent frame.
merge vs join: merge() on columns, join() on index. Use suffixes=('_x', '_y') when column names collide.

common_patterns.read_streamflow_csv:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('streamflow.csv', parse_dates=['date'], index_col='date')
df = df.sort_index()
df = df[~df.index.duplicated(keep='first')]
